narrative.overview:
The page is a quiet, near-white warm sheet. Everything the child works with is a white sticker card lifted off it: a white keyline ring and a soft lilac drop. Reading text always sits on the plain white sticker. The one playful block is the page band: a full-width pale lilac block (#E7DFFF; dark #3A2E7A) behind every screen title, curved at the bottom (2rem), carrying a quiet static confetti tile that is masked to fade out under the title so no shape sits behind text. Deep navy ink, a sunrise orange primary, and saturated book-jacket cloth that owns whole regions. The owl (purple #8A6FF0 app-icon tile) is the single character, and it speaks through a small speech tag.

The system is calm and low-density in its controls: one thing burns brightest at a time, and nothing loops. Dark mode is a deep-violet night sheet with the same structure: #1B1633 ground, #2A2350 sticker cards, a #3A2E7A band with white ink and faint confetti. Browser toolbar color follows the band (#E7DFFF light, #3A2E7A dark).
keyCharacteristics: One vertical rhythm: `--pitch` sets reading line-height and row height at every font-size setting, even though the sheet is no longer ruled.
Quiet warm-white ground, a lilac confetti page band behind each title, white keylined sticker cards, navy ink, flat cloth-colored jackets, one orange accent.
One character family: owl (idle, cheer, think, wave, sleep; outfits none, glasses, cap, bow) across flat art, 3D, covers, stickers and empty states.
State by shape first (circle/square/triangle difficulty stamps), color only reinforces.
Offline-to-AI upgrades restyle in place with reserved space, no layout shift.
Motion is transform and opacity, 140-300ms, once per flow, off under reduced motion; no looping decoration.
Large targets (44px minimum, 48-60px for actions) for ages 6-12.

rules.name: The One Burner Rule
rules.body: Orange goes on the single in-page primary action and the tapped word. The raised Scan button in the nav is a deliberate, user-approved second occurrence because Scan is the product's primary action everywhere; do not extend that exception to other controls.

rules.name: The Mixed-Tint Rule
rules.body: Reading overlays (yellow, blue, pink) are mixed into the white sticker sheet (`card-surface`) at 12-16% and never laid over text, so ink contrast holds. Contrast pairs are asserted in `src/styles/contrast.test.ts`; change a token only with that test green.

rules.name: The Label-on-Cloth Rule
rules.body: The notebook label stuck on a book cover is paper on cloth and stays light in dark mode; only the surrounding sheet darkens. (Sticker cards themselves do darken to #2A2350.)

rules.name: The Plain-Sheet Rule
rules.body: Reading text sits only on the plain white sticker card.

rules.name: The Band-Only Confetti Rule
rules.body: Confetti lives only in the page band (.page-band, 2rem bottom radius), never on the page ground or a card, and never behind text: the tile is masked empty under the title. Static, no animation.

rules.name: The Pitch Rule
rules.body: Reading text uses `.pad-text`, whose line-height is `--pitch` (2.25rem, 2.5rem at lg). Sizes are rem-based and the html font-size class scales pitch and text together, so line and row heights stay one rhythm. There is no ruling to align to.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels are sentence case, bold, small. No uppercase tracked labels, no kickers or eyebrows above titles.

rules.name: The Named Step Rule
rules.body: Off-scale sizes exist only as the named steps above (helper, example, word title small, display-desktop, nav label at Large text). Add a new literal size only by adding a step here.

rules.name: The Soft Navy Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are blurred, offset-down, and navy-tinted (black in dark). The one exception is the sticker drop, a lilac, unblurred offset that is the sticker device itself; no other hard offset shadows or glow.

rules.name: The Sticker Rule
rules.body: A card that carries content is a sticker: `--card-surface` fill, the `--sticker` keyline and drop. The keyline is part of the sticker, not a second border.

rules.name: The Sink Rule
rules.body: The `pressable` utility gives every tappable thing a pointer cursor, `touch-action: manipulation`, a 140ms transition and a 2px downward press (motion-safe); pressed shadow tokens accompany it. Hover colors apply only on hover-capable pointers.

dos: **Do** read tokens only from the CSS custom properties / Tailwind utilities (`bg-paper`, `text-ink`, `bg-sunrise`, `shadow-cta`, `shadow-tile`).
**Do** put a page band behind every screen title (PageHeader, skeletons included).
**Do** lay reading text on `.pad` / `.pad-text` (the white sticker sheet) so line-height equals the pitch.
**Do** pair every difficulty color with its shape (circle, square, triangle) and label.
**Do** use ink navy text on sunrise and mango, white on indigo, kangkong, and gumamela.
**Do** gate every GSAP helper (enterPanel, markWord, stampIn, fadeRoute) and every celebration on reduced motion and animate only transform and opacity.
**Do** reserve space for content that upgrades in place.
**Do** use `pressable` on every tappable thing, and letter tiles instead of emoji in lists.
**Do** load optional heavy pieces (3D owl, rewards, celebration) through `softDynamic` so a failure falls back silently.
**Do** show locked stickers as washed art with a lock chip.
**Do** keep owl-voice and sticker copy short; it awaits native-speaker review in Hiligaynon and Tagalog.
donts: **Don't** add a second sunrise action on a screen beyond the nav Scan button.
**Don't** put a loop on decoration; the only ambient motion is the owl's occasional blink and glance and the capped 3D sleep bob.
**Don't** use candy gradients, stacked stat tiles, or emoji as chrome.
**Don't** put a color overlay over text; mix it into the sticker sheet.
**Don't** put confetti anywhere but the page band, behind any text, or animate it.
**Don't** use hard offset shadows or glow.
**Don't** load the 3D owl on slow, save-data, very low-end or software-WebGL devices, or under reduced motion.
**Don't** name a control differently from its visible text.
**Don't** put a timer on the Pares game.
